correct_answer: Real 22% price increase correctly reflected. The vendor's 2026 price schedule shows $48.70/C = $0.487/EA. The SAP info record's previous price of $0.399/EA matches the old Oracle price of $39.85/C converted correctly. The migration was done right; the plant manager is wrong.
rationale: The vendor's email is the critical external signal that resolves the apparent contradiction. Continental Fasteners quotes prices in $/C (per hundred), consistent with how Oracle stored them. Their 2026 schedule shows $48.70/C for this part, which converts to $0.487/EA — exactly matching the current SAP price. Their previous price was $39.85/C = $0.3985/EA, which rounds to the SAP info record's previous price of $0.399/EA. The migration WAS performed correctly for this item: Oracle's $398.50/C is actually $39.85/C (the Oracle system stored values in tenths of cents, a display format issue Lisa was confusing in the Teams DM). The 22% increase ($39.85 to $48.70 per C) is real and due to the zinc surcharge the vendor documented. Answer A incorrectly assumes a migration error based on the misleading Teams DM where Lisa confused herself mid-calculation. Answer C invents a 10x error that doesn't exist — it misreads the Oracle price format. Answer D is the failure mode of giving up when multiple signals actually do converge on a clear answer once the vendor's pricing email is consulted as the external source of truth.
